🧠 Crypto News Brief: A ceasefire pause did more for crypto today than crypto did. Bitcoin reclaimed $65,000 as oil collapsed and ether ran at it — while behind the rally, exchanges keep switching off the lights. 🕊️ Iran–U.S. Ceasefire Pause Lifts Crypto as Oil Tumbles The U.S. and Iran paused strikes around the Strait of Hormuz for a second consecutive day, sending Brent crude down more than 7% to roughly $87 and easing the inflation fear that has weighed on risk assets for weeks. Bitcoin climbed back above $65,000 and ether outperformed at about $1,963, nearing $2,000 for the first time since early June. DeFi names led the bounce, with AAVE up 9% and ONDO up 7%. Markets now price a 30.5% chance of a Fed hike on Wednesday, down from 37.4% at Friday's close. Read full story 🏛️ Clarity Act Down to Its Final Two Weeks in the Senate Senators released fresh text of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, merging the Banking and Agriculture Committee drafts and, for the first time, spelling out an ethics provision that would bar senior officials from sponsoring or issuing their own cryptocurrencies. The window is closing fast: the Senate leaves town in two weeks, and Democrats still want a more binding version of that provision than the White House has agreed to. Prediction markets currently lean against passage in 2026. More details 📊 Bitcoin ETFs Book a Third Straight Weekly Inflow U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs closed a third consecutive week of net inflows, even after shedding $465 million in the closing sessions. BlackRock's IBIT drove the vast majority of the late-week reversal, accounting for close to $415 million of the outflows on its own. The pattern points to institutional demand that is holding up in aggregate but is now heavily concentrated in a single product — and increasingly reactive to macro headlines rather than crypto-native ones. Read more 🏚️ BitMart Winds Down After Nine Years, BMX Collapses BitMart announced an orderly wind-down of its trading platform, halting new registrations, deposits and orders immediately, ending all spot and derivatives trading on August 26, and closing entirely on January 31, 2027. Its BMX token fell roughly 58% in 24 hours, extending a decline of about 70% over the past year. The exchange, which recently reported $1.6 billion in daily volume, is keeping withdrawals open but warns of extended identity and sanctions

Gm data enjoyers! We hope everyone's been having a wonderful summer. O ur team recently set up a new newsletter titled " Tokenization Briefing ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters )." With trillions of dollars of real-world assets migrating onto blockchain rails, we are introducing a way for readers to keep up to date with market insights and visual analyses on what matters in the world of Tokenization. Sign up here ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters ).

This week, we’re taking a look at STRC and Ethereum rollups. We’ll also look at Stablecoins, Robinhood chain, and Pump.fun data. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let's dive in.

1: Still Out STRC’d

( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/public-companies/strategys-preferred-stocks-volumes )

Chart via The Block's Data Dashboard

*Key Insights* provided by The Block Research

* Strategy’s preferred stock STRC has had volume stall, now trading less than a million dollars a day, a steep drop from its peak where it was doing north of $10 million.

* STRC closed Friday at $86, the first close of the monthly VWAP that Strategy will use to determine the management recommendation of how much to raise the dividend for STRC.

* The preferred stock has yet to trade above $90 this month, well off the $100 target the company has cited as its range. With 5 trading days left this week, it's likely that the VWAP will come in below $95, and Strategy will recommend a dividend raise of at least 0.5%.

* As a reminder, if the VWAP trades between $95-$98.99, the management recommendation is a raise by at least 0.25 percentage points.
Each 25bp increase adds roughly $26 million to Strategy's annual obligations, so the minimum move would run around $53 million a year, stacking onto a rate that's already gone from 9% at launch to 12% across seven hikes.

* Strategy has shown it's been willing to defend STRC by selling equity even at compressed mNAV to fund STRC’s dividend.

See the Interactive Chart ( https://www.theblock.co/data/crypto-markets/public-companies/strategys-preferred-stocks-volumes )

Welcome back! A theme runs through everything this week: the biggest wins are coming from cutting, not adding. Anthropic deleted most of its system prompt, NVIDIA got frontier results from a 253-line agent, a new index shrinks vectors 16x and the right fine-tuning framework beats the biggest one.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Anthropic removed 80% of Claude Code's system prompt with no measurable loss, and the new rules of context engineering NVIDIA's NOOA makes an agent a plain Python object, hitting 82.2% on SWE-bench from 253 lines TurboVec squeezes 31GB of embeddings into 4GB with zero training, beating FAISS by 8-9 points Unsloth vs Axolotl vs TRL vs LLaMA-Factory: which fine-tuning framework fits your hardware PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Anthropic deleted 80% of Claude Code's system prompt and nothing broke  Anthropic just shared something counterintuitive:  They removed over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt for the newest Claude 5 models (Opus 5 and Fable 5) with no measurable loss on their coding evals.  The lesson is a rethink of context engineering, everything Claude sees beyond your prompt:  system prompt, Skills, CLAUDE.md, memory. The core realization: they'd been over-constraining Claude.  Their own transcripts showed single requests carrying conflicting instructions, "leave documentation as appropriate" fighting "DO NOT add comments."  Older models needed those hard guardrails. Newer ones have the judgment to read context and decide well without them. Each old rule flipped: → Rigid rules, now judgment. "Never write multi-line comments" became "write code that reads like the surrounding code."  → Examples, now interface design. Examples box the model in, so expressive tool parameters teach better than a sample.  → Everything upfront, now progressive disclosure. Load verification and review only when needed; defer tool definitions until searched.  → Repeat yourself, now simple tool descriptions.  → Manual memory, now auto-memory.  → Simple specs, now rich references like test suites and rubrics. 76559.subject: The NFT Slot Machine
76559.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

Hi everyone. Markets rallied broadly over the past 24 hours, led by lending protocols and Ethereum ecosystem tokens as EVM activity continued to strengthen. We also take a closer look at one of CT’s hottest new protocols, Fake World Assets, where NFT gacha mechanics have already generated more than $14M of activity in just a few days. We examine how the model works, why activity has exploded, and whether its fee-driven flywheel can survive once emissions disappear. 

———————————————————————————

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/42e942ec-f31d-4957-8722-a3ac7b121e1e/0xR_NL_Market_Update.png?t=1767631151) [Market Update]
Caption: 

The board was almost entirely green over the last 24 hours. 21 of 25 crypto indices closed higher, the three equity-linked indices sat flat with US markets shut, and Solana Eco was the only decliner at -1.41%. Sectors climbed steadily through the European and US hours, faded into the evening, then gapped higher together in the closing stretch.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/698558fd-c46f-4a19-b23f-3ea7d9fbcb63/image.png?t=1785154794)
Caption: 

Lending led at 9.49%, with Ethereum Eco effectively tied at 9.45%. The two ran together all session on shared lending exposure, the same pairing that led the board last Wednesday. Euler was the standout component. EUL spiked 32% intraday and closed up roughly 14% after Upbit opened a KRW market for the token on Sunday, taking its gain on the week to about 90%.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7dafd668-7d7a-4651-be92-fcdd546cc84a/image.png?t=1785154794)
Caption: 

That left nearly 11 percentage points between Ethereum Eco and Solana Eco on the day, as EVM activity gained share through Robinhood Chain, with apps such as Pons [attracting](https://dune.com/adam_tehc/pons) onchain attention. 

— [Shaunda](https://x.com/shaundadevens)

———————————————————————————

# The NFT Gacha Experiment

This week, we take a look at one of Crypto Twitter's hottest new protocols, [Fake World Assets](https://www.fwa.fun/) (FWA). Think of it as bringing the gacha mechanics that have proven so successful on Collector Crypt to NFTs.

Depositors deposit an NFT together with some ETH, creating a position that purchasers can acquire at random by paying a fixed acquisition fee of 0.16 ETH.
